knownTraps: Do not infer Pi installation, provider readiness, privacy, or model delivery from configuration files.
Windows system bootstrap uses the exact tracked standalone release archive and digest; do not substitute a user-global npm Pi or arbitrary PATH executable.

Machine ownership stops at the Pi runtime, AgentSwitchboard launchers, and Machine PATH entry. Provider authentication, Pi settings, project trust, sessions, and model preferences remain user/project scoped.
The npm workstation preflight is a compatibility/adoption probe; it is not the Windows system-bootstrap dependency floor.
Record bounded npm/Pi command-path evidence because Windows user-level shims may coexist with the managed Program Files runtime.
Honor a reviewed project-local Pi shellPath before Windows Git defaults or PATH fallbacks for interactive project use.
Do not configure every agent pair directly. Parents delegate bounded packets through the AgentSwitchboard child-invocation seam.
Read-only child agents may fan out; writer children require clean isolated worktrees, non-default branches, and one writer per mutation surface.
Raw Pi JSON event streams can contain prompt/model transcript data and must remain outside tracked repository authority.
Do not promote one-shot JSON child invocation to persistent RPC until LF framing, cancellation, session isolation, and result-envelope behavior have executable tests.
Do not run autovalidation without attempt, wall-clock, token, cancellation, and no-progress bounds.
proofCeiling: Repository contracts and CI can prove exact tracked release identity, system-bootstrap implementation, bounded child-invocation guards, and deterministic workflow semantics. Physical machine installation, provider authentication, model response, child-agent quality, actual parallel fan-out, fusion/autovalidation delivery, and deployment require separate runtime evidence.
